items.stem: Under the SAE levels of driving automation, what is the key distinction of Level 3 compared with Level 2?

options.text: At Level 3 no driver is ever required in the vehicle
options.rationale: That describes higher levels; Level 3 still relies on a fallback-ready user.

options.text: At Level 3 the system performs the full driving task within its ODD and the driver need not monitor continuously, but must take over when requested
options.rationale: Level 3 is conditional automation: within its ODD the driver can disengage from monitoring but must resume control on a takeover request.

options.text: Level 3 and Level 2 are identical in required driver attention
options.rationale: They differ precisely in monitoring requirements.

options.text: Level 3 removes all sensors from the vehicle
options.rationale: Higher automation requires more capable sensing, not none.

items.explanation: Level 3 is conditional automation: within its ODD the driver can disengage from monitoring but must resume control on a takeover request.

items.stem: Why is radar often fused with cameras in ADAS perception?

options.rationale: Radar does not provide colour or high spatial resolution; cameras do.

options.text: Radar measures range and closing speed robustly in poor visibility, complementing the camera's rich but weather-sensitive imagery
options.rationale: Radar's direct range and velocity sensing in rain, fog and darkness complements the camera's detailed but light-dependent data.

options.text: Radar is only used for infotainment
options.rationale: Radar is a perception sensor, not an entertainment feature.

options.text: Cameras cannot detect anything at all
options.rationale: Cameras are highly capable; fusion combines complementary strengths.

items.explanation: Radar's direct range and velocity sensing in rain, fog and darkness complements the camera's detailed but light-dependent data.

items.stem: A validation lead reviews an ADAS feature before release. Select TWO limitations that are important to communicate honestly about a Level 2 system.

options.text: The driver remains responsible and must supervise continuously
options.rationale: Level 2 requires constant driver supervision; this must be made clear.

options.text: Performance can degrade outside the defined operational design domain
options.rationale: Behaviour is only assured within the ODD, so limits must be stated honestly.

options.text: The system is fully autonomous and needs no driver
options.rationale: That is false for Level 2 and dangerous to imply.

options.text: The system has been proven safe in every possible scenario
options.rationale: No finite test campaign proves safety in every scenario.

options.text: Sensors work identically in all weather and lighting
options.rationale: Sensor performance varies with conditions, so this claim is false.

items.explanation: Level 2 requires constant driver supervision; this must be made clear.
